title: Chromosomal Disorders (Aneuploidy, Structural Defects)
objectives: Classify chromosomal abnormalities by type and mechanism
Correlate specific cytogenetic findings with clinical phenotypes

structural_abnormalities.title: Chromosomal Rearrangements
structural_abnormalities.content:
Deletions
• 22q11.2 del: DiGeorge syndrome
• 5p-: Cri-du-chat (high-pitched cry)
Translocations
• Robertsonian: 45,der(14;21) in Down carriers
• Reciprocal: t(9;22) in CML (BCR-ABL1)

diagnostic_methods.title: Testing Approaches
diagnostic_methods.content:
Karyotyping

Resolution: 5-10 Mb
Best for: Aneuploidy, large rearrangements
Turnaround: 7-14 days

Chromosomal Microarray

Resolution: 50-100 kb
Detects: CNVs, UPD, consanguinity
First-line for: DD/ID, MCA

counseling_points.title: Recurrence Risks
counseling_points.content:
• Non-disjunction: 1% baseline + maternal age adjustment
  • Balanced translocation carrier: 5-30% risk for unbalanced offspring
  • 22q11.2 deletion: 50% risk if parent affected (AD)

case_studies.title: Clinical Correlations
case_studies.content:
Prader-Willi Syndrome

Mechanism: Paternal 15q11-13 del (70%)
Testing: Methylation analysis
Key feature: Neonatal hypotonia → childhood hyperphagia

Williams Syndrome

Deletion: 7q11.23 (ELN gene)
Features: Supravalvular AS, social personality
Testing: FISH or CMA

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why does advanced maternal age increase aneuploidy risk?

Oocytes remain in prophase I for decades - accumulated meiotic errors and weakened cohesin proteins increase non-disjunction (especially chr21).

How can a balanced translocation cause problems?

Breakpoints may disrupt genes, or meiosis can produce unbalanced gametes (adjacent-1 segregation → 50% abnormal).

Why is microarray better than karyotype for autism?

Detects smaller CNVs (e.g., 16p11.2 del/dup) and UPD - yields 15-20% diagnosis rate vs 3% with karyotype.
